analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift: artifact hashing and cache eligibility (552–641), native ownership, memory admission and slot publication (660–1014), unload/drain and reserve accounting (1092–1443), and request admission/error sanitization (1475–1660). Considered the full threat index, especially T-012/T-027 artifact substitution, T-041 cache bindings, T-028 residual memory, T-010/T-029 availability, and T-053 authorization lifetime. No independently supported regression is established by these BASE-only source units.
The bounded patch introduces loadWeightHasher indirection and describes managed GLM manifest verification replacing load-bracketing hash observations. Integration must inspect the actual HEAD implementation at changed ranges 542–563 and 615–658, the hasher's production initialization, and GLM5NextManagedLoad/manifest ownership contracts: confirm the substituted digest identifies the bytes actually loaded, mutation fails before publication, and the digest remains compatible with SSD model binding and coordinator-visible hashes. BASE 606–620 previously brackets eligible loads with fresh hashes; BASE 754–755 and 940–941 propagate artifact/cache identities into the engine and slot. Missing HEAD behavior here prevents validating that security-sensitive replacement; it is not evidence of a missing control. Existing ownership-aware unwind, retirement, memory guards, and sanitized loadInferenceFailure are surrounding behavior, not new findings. No supplied change establishes altered transport encryption, attestation, token custody, fan privileges, or billing controls; their unchanged callers were not examined.
